current_answer: NLnet policy v2.0, effective 20 October 2026, changes the application gate for the open CodeSupply and Restack calls. Applicants may not use generative AI to write proposals, except disclosed assistance needed for accessibility. Funded deliverables cannot be AI-generated; read-only checks are allowed with transparency. The 3 November, 12:00 CET call remains open. CodeSupply’s EUR 5,000–50,000 first-project request is competitive and paid after milestones, not in advance.

catalogue_card.question: Can you use AI to prepare NLnet’s 3 November grant application?
catalogue_card.text: NLnet’s 20 October policy v2.0 says no AI proposal writing or idea generation for CodeSupply and Restack, except disclosed accessibility assistance. Read-only checks may be used during funded development; AI-generated deliverables cannot. The 3 November, noon CET call remains open.

summary: Policy v2.0 applies to the current Restack and CodeSupply calls despite older form disclosure text and archived Q&A.
Applicants who wrote a proposal with AI before 20 October need not resubmit solely for that writing; proposed work that conflicts with v2.0 can be revised before the deadline.
CodeSupply remains a competitive EUR 5,000–50,000 first-project request for open-source software supply-chain work; payment follows completed milestones.
uncertainty: Applicant-specific interpretation of borderline read-only use, accessibility support and significant pre-existing generated code remains with NLnet.
No application was submitted or award verified; first-party analytics and applicant outcomes are unavailable.
